title: 中国人怎么吃一只鸡④完结·叫花鸡：一身泥，剥开却是名菜 | How China Eats a Chicken P4 · Beggar's Chicken 🔥
description:
大盘鸡、白切鸡、口水鸡、叫花鸡——你家乡的一只鸡，怎么吃？

中国人怎么吃一只鸡 第④集·完结 · 常熟叫花鸡。这道后来能上宴席的名菜，相传是乞丐发明的：清代常熟，一个叫花子偶得一只鸡，既无锅又无调料，便去掉内脏、用荷叶包裹再糊上黄泥，丢进柴火里煨。等泥巴烤干、鸡也熟了，摔开泥壳，连鸡毛都随壳脱落，香气四溢。约100多年前，常熟虞山「山景园」菜馆据这个传说精工创制，后因传说受皇帝赞赏而得名「富贵鸡」，从乞丐的吃食登上大雅之堂。

从新疆公路边的大盘鸡，到广东宴席的白切鸡、四川凉拌的口水鸡，再到裹泥火煨的叫花鸡——一只鸡，装得下四种中国。

Beggar's chicken (jiao hua ji), a banquet delicacy today, was reportedly invented by a beggar: in Qing-dynasty Changshu, a vagrant got hold of a chicken but had no pot or seasoning, so he gutted it, wrapped it in lotus leaves and yellow clay, and buried it in a wood fire. When the clay baked hard and the bird cooked through, he smashed the shell open — feathers peeling away with it — and the aroma spread. About a century ago, the Shanjingyuan restaurant on Changshu's Yushan refined the legend into a dish; a story that an emperor praised it earned the polite name "Rich Chicken." From Xinjiang's roadside big-plate, to Canton's plain white-cut, to Sichuan's chili-soaked drool chicken, to this clay-baked bird — one chicken holds four Chinas.
